transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-11-04 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Priya Shah (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Maya Ruiz (Redwood SE), Daniel Price (Palmetto Head of Eng), Anita Gomez (Palmetto Security Lead), Leo Tan (Platform Architect), Sara Mitchell (Product)

Summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Palmetto is evaluating Redwood for inference powering quoting and risk models. Primary constraints: log retention rules, redaction prior to leaving their VPC, and KMS key residency (must remain in EU for EU accounts). They prefer Dedicated but need private control plane or on-prem option for auditability. Action items and next steps captured.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Priya Shah: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Priya from Redwood, AE on the account. Quick round robin?
[00:07] Daniel Price: Daniel here, Palmetto — head of eng. We'll mostly listen but Leo and Anita have the details.
[00:12] Anita Gomez: Anita, security. Hi.
[00:13] Leo Tan: Leo, platform architect.
[00:14] Sara Mitchell: Sara, product. I'll take notes.
[00:17] Priya Shah: Awesome. Ethan and Maya from our SE team are on for technicals. We'll run a few discovery questions and then get into logging, KMS, residency.
[00:25] Ethan Cole: Hi all. Quick note — if you have a compliance doc you want to drop in the chat we can reference it after.
[00:30] Anita Gomez: Will do. The high level is: we need to ensure EU customer data never leaves EU infrastructure, keys are EU-resident, and logs sent to your control plane must be redacted or never contain PII.
[00:44] Maya Ruiz: Understood. When you say logs, are you including request/response body logs, or just metadata and request headers?
[00:51] Anita Gomez: Both potentially. Our legal says request/response bodies could contain customer identifiers or partial trade details, so default is assume bodies are not allowed off-prem unless redacted.
[01:05] Ethan Cole: Got it. That's pretty common. We have a few options — Hosted with data residency controls, Dedicated (reserved capacity) in EU region where data and logs remain in-region, or Private deployment where control plane is in your VPC or on-prem. Each has different tradeoffs for speed of onboarding and operational overhead.
[01:25] Daniel Price: Can you explain the distinction you'd recommend for us? We're leaning Dedicated but want clarity on KMS and auditability.
[01:32] Priya Shah: Dedicated gives you a dedicated pool of GPUs in our infra in the region you pick, with stronger isolation and contract terms. For KMS, we offer integrations where you can bring your own KMS keys in some Dedicated/private options — Ethan can give the specifics.
[01:44] Ethan Cole: For Dedicated in EU, we can do customer-managed keys where the master keys reside in the customer's KMS — either cloud KMS or HSM via a partner. That means we never have the key material. For Hosted standard, keys are managed by Redwood unless you upgrade to enterprise keystore options.
[02:00] Anita Gomez: So with Dedicated + BYOK, logs still leave your control plane? How are audit logs handled? We need full chain of custody for requests and evidence for auditors.
[02:12] Maya Ruiz: With Dedicated we can route logs to your logging sinks (e.g., your Splunk/ELK in your VPC) instead of forwarding everything to Redwood's central control plane. There's a configuration where metrics and minimal telemetry are shared, and the detailed request logs can be pushed directly to your sinks using secure forwarding.
[02:29] Leo Tan: That sounds promising. Is that push real-time? We need sub-minute tracing for some risk alerts.
[02:36] Ethan Cole: Yes, it's near realtime; there may be batching for efficiency but we've seen sub-30s for metric and trace propagation in Dedicated set-ups.
[02:44] Daniel Price: What about redaction? Can Redwood perform redaction before anything leaves our network?
[02:50] Maya Ruiz: Two approaches — 1) Best is client-side redaction where you sanitize requests before calling the API, so the payload never contains PII. 2) If you want Redwood to handle it, we can deploy a redaction layer in the private control plane that strips fields according to a ruleset before logs are stored or forwarded. That requires a Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) so you control that redaction layer.
[03:12] Anita Gomez: On the KMS point — we must ensure keys never transit outside EU. How do you support regional KMS bindings?
[03:20] Ethan Cole: We support binding model encryption and storage keys to regional KMS providers. For Dedicated with BYOK, you can provision keys in Google Cloud KMS or AWS KMS with regional-only policies; the key material never leaves that KMS. For Private, you can integrate an HSM or on-prem KMS. We also support key rotation hooks and audit events.
[03:37] Leo Tan: Any chance you support key escrow for regulatory requests? Our legal says for certain EU sub-entities we might need key escrow with a neutral third party.
[03:45] Priya Shah: We have partners for escrow — it's not standard but possible. We'll need the legal team to align; we can put that in the pilot terms.
[03:53] Anita Gomez: Logs retention: our auditors require 7 years for trading logs, but we want to redact anything PII after 30 days. Can Redwood support tiered retention with automated redaction at thresholds?
[04:05] Ethan Cole: We support tiered retention. The easiest pattern is: short-term full fidelity (e.g., 30 days), then redacted archived logs for longer retention. With Private or Dedicated plus your sink, you can keep full fidelity in your own storage; Redwood will only keep minimal telemetry.
[04:20] Daniel Price: If we use Hosted with region-lock options, are there any guarantees the control plane won't route failover traffic through US? We have to avoid US transit for EU data.
[04:30] Maya Ruiz: We have routing policies and region-lock features — you can require strict regional-only routing for both inference and fallback. That said, Hosted has more complexity with cross-region fallbacks; for strict regulatory constraints, Dedicated or Private is safer.
[04:44] Anita Gomez: Can you share SLA numbers for latency and availability on Dedicated? Our trading systems require low tail latency.
[04:51] Ethan Cole: Our Dedicated plans come with SLA-backed uptime and tail latency targets. For the GPU families we recommend for low-latency inference we publish p99 latency numbers under typical loads; I'll share the benchmark doc. For extreme low tail latencies we recommend a reserved pool with pinned worker nodes and continuous batching tuned to your QPS.
[05:10] Leo Tan: About batching — if you enable continuous batching to save cost, does that add jitter to p99? We have hard SLOs on order entry.
[05:18] Ethan Cole: Yes batching trades off cost vs latency. For order entry you probably want minimal batching, fine-grained routing, and possibly a dedicated subset of workers with smaller batch windows. We can configure hybrid policies: critical routes get minimal batching and fallback routes use aggressive batching.
[05:34] Anita Gomez: Auditability: our auditors want immutable logs with proof-of-origin. Do you handle signing logs or do we sign them before sending?
[05:43] Maya Ruiz: Both options exist. We can sign logs at source if deployed in your VPC, or we can accept signed records from your side. Redwood's control plane can also generate signed audit events but that requires private deployment to satisfy some regulators.
[05:58] Daniel Price: How intrusive is the Private deployment? What ops are we responsible for vs Redwood?
[06:03] Priya Shah: Private has two modes: VPC-hosted private control plane where Redwood manages the software but you control networking and keys, and full on-prem where you run the stack. In VPC-hosted private, we manage upgrades, and you manage networking, KMS, and the redaction layer; for on-prem you own everything and we'll provide support.
[06:20] Leo Tan: For pilot scope, what would you want from us? We can give sample traces and sequence lengths.
[06:26] Ethan Cole: Perfect — we'll need sample traffic pattern, sequence length distribution, QPS, expected concurrency, any heavy prompt templates, and your compliance checklist. We'll use that to recommend instance types, batching windows, and the deployment pattern.
[06:39] Anita Gomez: One more on logs: even metadata like user IDs can be sensitive. Can we enforce that the API never logs headers or IPs outside our sinks?
[06:49] Maya Ruiz: Yes, we can configure minimal telemetry to strip headers and IPs. We'll put that in the pilot security profile.
[06:55] Sara Mitchell: Quick question — cost angle. If we go Dedicated with BYOK and log forwarding to our S3, will that increase Redwood charges?
[07:03] Priya Shah: Primary cost drivers are instance-hour costs for Dedicated and data egress for any data we forward. If you host logs in your S3 there's no Redwood egress; if Redwood forwards to your sink over a secure tunnel there may be a small forwarding fee for observability add-ons. We'll share pricing details.
[07:18] Daniel Price: Good. Any competitors we should be wary of? Our vendor eval team mentioned Anthropic and some private-cloud vendor.
[07:24] Priya Shah: Commonly mentioned are Anthropic and OpenAI for hosted models, and a few self-hosted inference vendors for private setups. We position on predictability and the ops tooling to make Dedicated/Private manageable.
[07:36] Anita Gomez: For HIPAA overlap — we have a small team working with health-insurance customers. Do you support HIPAA BAAs for Dedicated?
[07:44] Ethan Cole: Yes, we offer BAAs for Dedicated and Private contracts, with the right controls around keystore and audit logs. Hosted standard is trickier but possible with enterprise terms.
[07:55] Leo Tan: Ok that's helpful. Let's talk timeline — we need this in prod for an EU trading desk pilot by end of Q1. Could we do a Dedicated pilot in December?
[08:05] Priya Shah: We can aim for December pilot kickoff, subject to legal and paperwork. Action items: we'll send pilot docs and terms; Ethan will send perf benchmarks and a recommended topology; Palmetto will send compliance checklist and sample traffic.
[08:22] Daniel Price: Thanks. Anything else?
[08:24] Sara Mitchell: Not from product. We'll collate and follow up.
[08:28] Priya Shah: Great. Recap of next steps — Priya sends pricing/terms, Ethan shares benchmarks, Palmetto provides checklist and patterns, schedule deep dive week of 11/15.
[08:40] Anita Gomez: I'll share the compliance doc after the call.
[08:43] Priya Shah: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites and the doc bundle.
[08:47] Meeting ends

Notes on transcript quality: Some speaker overlaps and occasional word swap (e.g., "keystore" transcribed as "key store" in places). Timestamps are approximate.
